Product case study · Food delivery

Swiggy helps people find food.
Autopilot finishes the decision.

A constraint-aware ordering agent that turns a meal need into three transparent, ready-to-order carts—lifting conversion and frequency without relying on deeper discounts.

01
Frame the opportunity

Grow frequency before chasing bigger baskets.

Revenue model
MTUpeople who order
×
Frequencyorders per user
×
AOVvalue per order

GOVplatform demand

Swiggy monetizes the resulting demand through restaurant commissions, user fees, memberships and advertising. More local order density can also improve delivery economics.

Strategic insight

The habit gap is larger than the discovery gap.

Most historical users are not monthly transactors. A product that reliably closes recurring meal missions can create more value than another browse surface.

Chosen business lever

Incremental completed orders per eligible user.

Conversion is the immediate mechanism; 30-day order frequency is the durable outcome.

02
Define the user problem

The friction is between intent and confidence.

A
Primary user

Aarav, 29 · Bengaluru

Orders after work, values protein and price, but rarely begins with a restaurant in mind.

“I know the constraints—two people, one vegetarian, under ₹700, before 8:15. I don’t know which of 300 menus solves that.”
MomentUser work todayFailure modeMetric affected
IntentTranslate hunger into a dish or cuisineVague need, no starting pointEarly exits
DiscoveryScroll and filter restaurant listsChoice overloadTime to cart
EvaluationCompare price, rating, ETA and quantityInformation scattered across screensAdd-to-cart rate
CheckoutValidate fees, offers and final totalBudget surprise creates hesitationOrder conversion
RepeatRebuild the same decision next weekPast dishes remembered; context forgotten30-day frequency
Problem statement

For high-intent users without a restaurant in mind, Swiggy behaves like a marketplace to navigate—not a meal outcome to complete.

03
Design the intervention

From open intent to a valid cart in one decision.

1

Say the outcome

People, dietary needs, budget, mood and deadline in natural language.

2

Generate valid carts

AI interprets intent; deterministic systems verify menus, price, offers and ETA.

3

Choose one cart

Best match, best value or fastest—each with all-in cost and a clear reason.

4

Save the mission

Turn a successful occasion into a voluntary, editable routine.

Existing discovery

Query → recommendations

  • Finds dishes and restaurants
  • User still builds the meal
  • Price becomes clear late
  • Optimizes relevance
Swiggy Autopilot

Mission → validated cart

  • Solves multi-person constraints
  • Assembles a complete meal
  • Shows all-in price immediately
  • Optimizes confident completion
MVP includes
  • Text, voice and quick-chip intent capture
  • Three single-restaurant carts
  • All-in price, ETA and fit explanations
  • Item swap before checkout
  • Explicit routine save after success
Deliberate non-goals
  • No autonomous payment
  • No unverified allergy or nutrition claims
  • No cross-restaurant fulfilment
  • No invisible sponsored ranking
  • No unsolicited recurring orders

05
Make the AI credible

Use language models for intent—not for transactional truth.

User input“Dinner for two, one veg, high protein, under ₹700 by 8:15.”
→
1 · Intent parserLLM → structured constraintsParty, budget, diet, exclusions, deadline
→
2 · Candidate retrievalCatalog + availabilityMenus, stock, location, restaurant eligibility
→
3 · Cart optimizerRank complete combinationsFit, cost, portions, ETA, reliability, economics
→
4 · Transaction validatorDeterministic truth layerLive price, offer, fee, item and ETA validation
→
OutputThree explainable, purchasable carts
Price integrity

Show the payable total after known taxes, fees and offers; refresh before checkout.

Dietary safety

Never infer allergens. Show restaurant-provided information and ask when uncertain.

Commercial integrity

Sponsored options must meet constraints, remain clearly labelled and never suppress a better organic match.

User agency

No silent cart changes, automatic payments or recurring orders without explicit confirmation.

06
De-risk before scaling

Prove incrementality, trust and unit economics.

Testable hypothesis

For high-intent users without a restaurant in mind, three complete all-inclusive carts will cut median time-to-cart by ≥50% and improve completed-order conversion by 3–5% relative, without worsening cancellation rate or contribution margin.

Targets are hypotheses to calibrate against internal baselines—not claimed results.
ControlCurrent discovery experience
TreatmentAutopilot entry + three generated carts
EligibilityGeneric intent, long browse or cross-menu comparison
Read windowSession conversion + 30-day frequency
0–4 weeks

Discover

Funnel analysis, 20–30 interviews and human-concierge cart tests.

5–10 weeks

MVP

One city, dinner occasion, single restaurant and voluntary entry.

11–16 weeks

Learn

Preference memory, better portions, reliability ranking and experiment iteration.

Later

Expand

Saved routines, family profiles, group constraints and cross-service meal missions.

90-second close

“Swiggy’s existing AI helps users search. Autopilot goes one step further: it completes the meal decision. The user states the outcome—people, budget, preferences and time—and receives three complete, live-validated carts with transparent total prices. This directly improves the discovery-to-cart experience, reduces checkout hesitation and converts successful meal occasions into repeatable routines. The result is not just fewer taps; it is higher conversion, greater order frequency and more valuable high-intent traffic, protected by deterministic pricing, explicit sponsorship and user confirmation.”
